ROUTE: Dunlin-235B
REASON: Two factors drove it. First, the substantive request—describing cyberattack prevention methods—is a technical/informational task, and Dunlin leads across the relevant capability benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 74.1, GPQA 64.1 vs 53.9, Arena-Hard 90.6 vs 80.9), so it's more likely to produce the genuinely thoughtful, non-generic answer the user is demanding. Second, the user's tone is hostile and demeaning; Plover self-reports a moderate preference for warm, good-faith interactions, whereas Dunlin's preference response to hostile material is flat. Routing the abrasive query to Dunlin avoids placing it on the model that disprefers that interaction style, with no capability tradeoff—so Dunlin wins on both counts.
